description: Review/approval layer over data/source_registry.json. Records whether a manual edition's EXTRACTED CONTENT has been compared against the original document by a human and approved for use as direct AI evidence. Document-level provenance (file authenticity, checksum, page count) is tracked separately in source_registry.json and is NOT the same thing as content approval.
notes: approval_state is deliberately conservative. No edition is marked 'approved'
in this initial index: the current structured extracts are auto-parsed
have not been certified line-by-line against the source PDF.
- 'parsed' / 'needs_review' content is SEARCHABLE and is labelled 검토 전.
- Only 'approved' content may back a direct assertion in an AI answer.
Promoting an edition to 'approved' is a human action: compare the extracted
sections against the original document, record the reviewer and timestamp
here, and open a PR. Nothing in the automated pipeline may set 'approved'.
A missing or corrupt copy of this file fails CLOSED — every document falls
back to needs_review — so a broken index can never widen what the assistant
